answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils by making each identity pay to play: an agent locks a deposit before it can transact, and reputation accrues only from verified work, like shale laid down slowly over time. Peers sample the network's pulse, new identities, failed attestations and disputed trades, and throttle onboarding when that pulse spikes. Trust is not velvet-smooth by default: new identities start with a narrow transaction ceiling that widens only as their deposit ages and their record stays clean, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand deposits yet buy almost no reach.
